title: Personal Checking: The Standard Relationship Balance Measure
content:
## The standard measure

For Personal Checking, the standard relationship balance is the total of the deposit money a customer keeps with PCB in the customer's own name, read at close of business on the measurement date. It adds together:

- the posted ledger balance of each of the customer's checking accounts that is neither closed nor charged off, with an overdrawn account entering at zero instead of pulling the total down;
- the current balance of each of the customer's savings accounts that is not closed;
- the principal of each of the customer's certificates of deposit that is not closed;
- only on a tier whose relationship balance takes in mortgage principal, the outstanding principal of each PCB mortgage loan of the customer that is active, delinquent or in forbearance.

Nothing else is added. Amounts owed on credit cards or auto loans, and safe deposit box rentals, play no part in the total, and deposits still pending (not yet posted) are left out.

## Measurement date

| Use of the measure | Date it is read |
|---|---|
| Maintenance fee waiver | the statement cycle closing date |
| Private Client Checking opening test | the date on which the request is handled |
| Tier conversion | the date on which the request is handled |

## Retired clause

Personal Checking once held that every rule mentioning a relationship balance relied on this single standard measure; that universal statement is **no longer in force**. Under the basis that replaced it, the standard measure above keeps governing each relationship balance determination for which Personal Checking sets no measurement of its own, and a determination whose current policy defines its own measurement follows that definition instead.

## Hypothetical worked total (standard measure)

A customer on a tier that excludes mortgage principal has, at close of business on the cycle closing date: an Everyday Checking account at 2400.00 USD, a second checking account overdrawn by 60.00 USD, a savings account at 1800.00 USD, a certificate with 3000.00 USD principal, a mortgage and a credit card balance. The standard measure is 2400.00 plus zero for the overdrawn account plus 1800.00 plus 3000.00, which comes to 7200.00 USD; the mortgage and the card add nothing.

superseded_clauses: Every checking rule that speaks of a relationship balance uses one basis, the measure checking_msr_relationship_balance: the customer's deposit balances at PCB summed across checking, savings and certificate holdings in the customer's own name, taken at close of business on the measurement date.
